content.title: Server Components and Data Close to the Server
content.hook: Now use the boundary for something useful.
goals: Master Server Components and Data Close to the Server: browser asks → browser fetches → browser waits → browser renders

content.title: What changed?
content.text:
The component is now asynchronous.

Instead of:

**browser asks → browser fetches → browser waits → browser renders**

the application can perform work on the server before returning the rendered result.

content.question: Which component is the best candidate for server-side data access?

options.text: A component that only needs a click counter in the browser
A page that reads server-side application data and renders the result

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. A page that reads server-side application data and renders the result
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. A page that reads server-side application data and renders the result

content.title: Keep the client small
content.text:
Suppose the invoice list is large, but only a small filter control needs client-side interaction.

A strong architecture can look like:

```text
Server page
├── Server-rendered invoice data
└── Client filter control
```

The entire page does not need to become interactive.

content.title: Important boundary rule
content.text:
Do not place secrets into Client Components merely because the data is needed somewhere on the page.

Server-side work and client-side work have different visibility and trust properties.

The details of authentication and authorization come later.

For now, learn the architectural rule:

**Keep server-only work on the server.**

content.question:
A component needs an environment-only secret to query internal data.

Where should that work live?

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. In server-side code
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. In server-side code

content.title: Parallel work
content.text:
Suppose a server-rendered page needs two independent datasets:

```tsx
const [products, categories] = await Promise.all([
  getProducts(),
  getCategories(),
]);
```

The key idea is not the syntax.

The key idea is:

**Independent work does not always need to wait in sequence.**

content.question: Why can Server Components reduce client-side work?

options.text: They allow some rendering and data access to happen on the server instead of shipping all that work to the browser.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. They allow some rendering and data access to happen on the server instead of shipping all that work to the browser.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. They allow some rendering and data access to happen on the server instead of shipping all that work to the browser.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: The server/client boundary is not a limitation to fight.
It is a tool for deciding where work belongs.
nextSteps: Take one page that needs data and one interactive control. Sketch which parts should run on the server and which small part needs the client.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
